answer: Neighborhood quorum routing: each agent may route through only a small, slowly-rotating set of adjacent peers, and a new identity counts only when distinct existing peers independently place it in their routing tables. Because those placements compete for fixed slots, an attacker must convince many separate neighborhoods to displace real entries, paying coordination and reputation cost per identity. Like timber in a load path, trust flows only along verified edges, and each forged jade must be carried by an independent jetty before it counts.
